newsitem.title: USA: Allehgeny shareholders approve DQE merger.
newsitem.headline: Allehgeny shareholders approve DQE merger.

text.p: Allegheny Power System Inc shareholders have overwhelmingly approved the company's proposed merger with DQE Inc, Allegheny chief executive Alan Noia told a conference call on Thursday.
Earlier today, DQE shareholders also approved the proposed merger which will create an electric utility with an equity value of $6.2 billion.
Noia said that Allegheny had increased the company's estimate of stranded costs in Pennsylvania, the assets that might become unprofitable in a competitive market, to $2.0 billion from $500 million.
"The new number includes roughly $750 million of PURPA (Public Utilities Regulatory Policy Act costs)... and we now have a much better reading now on the market price of electricity," Noia said.
He said that a recent DQE study showed that the market price of electricity was about two cents per kilowatt hour and that its West Pennsylvania unit's cost of production was 3.5 cents.
DQE chief executive David Marshall said that savings from the merger would enable it to reduce the recovery time for its stranded costs by about a year.

Total estimated stranded costs for the 150 electric utilities in the United States are about $200 billion and the argument between utilities and regulators centers on to what extent those costs should be passed onto customers or absorbed by the companies.
The two companies still have to receive approval from numerous regulatory bodies, but expect to obtain final approval by May 1, 1998.
Both DQE and Allegheny have submitted return on equity targets of 11.5 percent to regulators as part of their rate filings, the companies said. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
